spots.name: Hanging Gardens of Babylon
spots.summary: The Hanging Gardens of Babylon were one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World listed by Hellenic culture.

spots.name: Ishtar Gate
spots.summary: The Ishtar Gate was the eighth gate to the inner city wall of Babylon. It was constructed c. 569 BC by order of King Nebuchadnezzar II on the north side of the city. It was part of a grand walled processional way leading into the city.

spots.name: Etemenanki

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Etemenanki was a Babylonian ziggurat dedicated to the Mesopotamian god Marduk. It is now in ruins, which are located about 90 kilometres (56 mi) south of Baghdad. Some scholars have proposed Etemenanki as the ziggurat that may have influenced the biblical account of the Tower of Babel.

spots.name: Esagila

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ésagila or Esangil was a temple dedicated to Marduk, the protector god of Babylon. It lay south of the ziggurat Etemenanki.

spots.name: Lion of Babylon
spots.summary: Lion of Babylon is a stone sculpture, over 2,600 years old, that was found in the ancient city of Babylon, Iraq. Its discovery was first documented in 1817 by Claudius Rich, although it may have been seen as early as 1790 by Joseph de Beauchamp.

spots.name: Euphrates Tunnel
spots.summary: The Euphrates Tunnel was a legendary tunnel purportedly built under the river Euphrates to connect the two halves of the city of Babylon in Mesopotamia.

spots.name: Saddam Hussein's Babylonian Summer Palace

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ridiculously over sized and out of place, the palace is one of the best examples of the former dictator's hubris. Situated on a hill overlooking the archaeological site, it provides excellent views. Visitors are free to wander within the palace and while some parts are covered in graffiti, many exquisite details such as ornaments remain intact.
